clue.text: Firms prepared to provide TLC

parts.note: COS is the plural of Co., company, so firms
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: Companies are getting ready to offer their staff some tender loving care.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper someone is to give them tender loving care, the meaning of TLC.

clue.text: Victor has to eat like a horse

explanation.surface: A winner needs to eat heartily.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion or winner is one sense; munching noisily as a horse does on its bit is the other.

clue.text: Pull up to correct electrical fault

explanation.surface: An electrician halts work to repair a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt suddenly is one sense; read literally, it means ending a short circuit.

clue.text: Woman writing article about South Africa

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A woman is writing a newspaper piece on South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, an example of a woman.

clue.text: Enterprising chap told to make the lady his!

indicators.note: told signals that the phrase is spoken aloud and heard, not read

parts.note: an instruction to win a woman over: go and win her, go get her

explanation.surface: An ambitious man is urged to win over the woman he fancies.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'go get her' sounds like the term for an ambitious achiever.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushy, ambitious person who chases success is called this.

clue.text: Admitted having lost on purpose

explanation.surface: Someone confessed to throwing the match deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal a secret is one sense; read literally, it means conceding a contest deliberately.

clue.text: Looks for glasses

explanation.surface: Someone searches for their spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Staring wide-eyed is one sense; protective eyewear is the other.

clue.text: Resented having got a complaint

explanation.surface: Someone took offence on catching an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something badly or amiss is one sense; falling sick with an ailment is the other, a medical sense of complaint.

clue.text: Sanguine compiler is certainly no mutt

parts.note: sanguine means blood-coloured, red
a setter compiles crosswords

explanation.surface: A cheerful crossword maker insists he is no fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutt' looks like an insult for a fool but means a mongrel dog; the answer is a pedigree Irish breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree Irish gundog with a chestnut coat is the opposite of a mongrel.

clue.text: Timber and mineral deposits on the coast

parts.note: ash is a hardwood tree and its timber
ore is rock containing metal or minerals

explanation.surface: Wood and ores lie strewn along a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land beside the sea, not afloat, is a synonym.

clue.text: Tramp offers Virginia and Georgia cement

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
to bond is to stick together, as cement does

explanation.surface: A homeless wanderer sells building cement in two southern US states.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant or wanderer with no fixed home is a synonym for a tramp.

clue.text: A chance to look for precious metals

explanation.surface: An opportunity arises to search for gold and silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A likelihood of success is one sense; searching ground for gold or silver deposits is the other, a mining verb.

clue.text: Liable to become unstable

indicators.note: to become something else, the letters of the clue word are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Something is prone to turn shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is signalled by 'to become': the clue's first word is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry and psychology the word describes something easily changed or not steady, a synonym.

clue.text: Subversion in the days when people wore clogs

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog worn by French peasants
an age is a period of time, as in 'in the days of'

explanation.surface: Wrecking was common back when everyone went about in wooden shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when people wore' is linking padding: read 'the days when people wore clogs' as a clog (SABOT) era (AGE). Legend says French workers threw sabots into machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate damage to undermine an enemy or employer is a form of subversion.

clue.text: Revolting slave from Greek city caught by us

parts.note: Sparta is an ancient Greek city
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A rebellious slave from a Greek city is captured by our side.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiator who led a slave rebellion against Rome in 73 BC.

clue.text: Retired coach allowed to extend tenancy

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for the coach is read backwards

parts.note: a coach is a bus
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: An old coach driver now out of work is permitted to stay on in the rented house.
explanation.definitionFit: To rent one's rented premises on to someone else passes on part of a lease, extending the tenancy to another.

clue.text: Latvian and I get extra port in America

parts.note: a Balt is a person from one of the Baltic states, such as Latvia
more means extra or additional

explanation.surface: A Latvian and I are offered more harbours across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A major seaport city in Maryland, USA, is an example.

clue.text: A mariner following King James Bible finds God on earth

indicators.note: following means the second part comes after the first, so the Bible version is put in front

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman reading his King James Bible discovers the divine in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief this is a deity's incarnation in bodily form on earth.

clue.text: Uncertain how ailing firms operate

explanation.surface: Nobody is sure how failing businesses keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Being puzzled or baffled is one sense; read literally, it is trading in the red, without profit.

clue.text: The farmer who hopes his stock is high

definitions.text: The farmer who hopes his stock is high

parts.words: The farmer who hopes his stock is high
parts.note: stock reads like stock market shares, but it means livestock, valued well by a cattle farmer

explanation.surface: A farmer investing in shares hopes their price climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer who runs a large cattle estate, whose stock is his herd.

clue.text: There's no confusion after the go-ahead

explanation.surface: Everything becomes plain once permission is given.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everything is understood, and also a signal that it is safe to proceed.

clue.text: Start getting the church roof stripped

explanation.surface: Thieves begin by stealing metal from a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin proceedings is one sense; read literally, old church roofs were covered in the metal and thieves strip it away.

clue.text: Roman emperor withdrew artillery before New Year

indicators.note: before places the turned artillery piece ahead of the month
withdrew means drew back, so the abbreviation for artillery is read backwards

parts.note: Art. is an abbreviation for artillery
January, abbreviated Jan, is the month that opens a new year

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler pulled his guns back before the year turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan ruled the Roman Empire from AD 98 to 117 and built the famous column.

clue.text: The inspector was once a pitman

parts.note: ex- describes something former, what was once
a pitman works down a coal pit, a miner

explanation.surface: A government inspector used to dig coal for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who tests or checks things is an inspector.

clue.text: French banker takes heart from your honesty

indicators.note: takes heart from means the letters are taken from the middle of the phrase

explanation.surface: A French bank manager is encouraged by a customer's honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A major river flowing through France has banks, so it is a banker in crossword terms.

clue.text: Dog needing double portion of food

indicators.note: double means the food word is written out twice

parts.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: The hound wants two helpings of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese breed of dog with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Loves to imbibe wine in Portugal

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the wine goes inside the pair of zeros

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O; two loves give OO
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Lovers drinking wine on holiday in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Porto in Portugal, home of port wine, is also known by this English name.

clue.text: How a nun feels towards her siblings

definitions.text: How a nun feels towards her siblings

parts.words: How a nun feels towards her siblings
parts.note: a nun is called Sister, and her fellow nuns are her sisters, so her feeling is the affection of a sibling

explanation.surface: A nun's attitude to her family.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means affectionate in the way a female sibling is, and a nun is a Sister.

clue.text: Charge exorbitant prices for sheepskin

explanation.surface: A shop overcharges for a woolly hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle or overcharge someone is one sense; the woolly coat of a sheep is the other.
